$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for the IDENTITY-ACCESS half of
compare-and-set precondition, tenant-isolation key, transaction boundary,
migration-only write invariant, unreadable-column refusal and scope
assembly rule in the ten stores, each carrying the file it lives in, the
EXACT text that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`),
and the NAMED cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
The twenty-two tranche-1 entries are in ./mutations.json and are unchanged.
This file is the tranche-2 half and is kept separate so the two tranches'
evidence can be read, and re-run, independently.
A guard nothing can turn red is a guard that is not there.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: the context's dist/ had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to LOAD and would have 'died' against no mutation at all. The driver
runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep unless it is green, and
classifies a module-load failure with no named failing case as VACUOUS
rather than as a kill.
For one entry: build @platos/tenancy-database, @platos/context-identity-access
and @platos/context-tenancy; replace its `from` with its `to` in the named
file; rebuild; run `pnpm exec vitest run <suites>` from the package with
DOCKER_HOST and TESTCONTAINERS_DOCKER_SOCKET_OVERRIDE set; confirm a NAMED
case goes red. Then revert, rebuild and confirm green.
A mutation the COMPILER rejects is recorded as KILLED-BY-COMPILER and is
counted separately from a kill by a case, because a type error is a
different kind of evidence from a failing assertion.
THIRTY OF THE THIRTY-SIX NEED A REAL POSTGRESQL -- every entry whose suites
end in `.integration.test.ts`. None of them could have been written against
a double: the conformance entries are about a conditional UPDATE affecting
zero rows on its second call, the constraint entries about rules that exist
only in the migrations, and the transaction entries about a write that has
to disappear when a later one fails.

result: THIRTY-SEVEN ENTRIES, THIRTY-SEVEN KILLS, NONE VACUOUS, on a real PostgreSQL
container at branch head. Each kill is a NAMED case in the `kills` list of its
entry, and the driver classified nothing as vacuous because it proved every
suite set green BEFORE mutating and treats a module-load failure with no named
failing case as vacuous rather than as a kill.
TWO ENTRIES SURVIVED THE FIRST SWEEP AND BOTH WERE FINDINGS, not noise:
M-I32 (loading only the first identity of every end user) survived because
every seeded end user in the conformance scenario had exactly ONE identity,
so `take: 1` was indistinguishable from loading them all. The FIXTURE was at
fault; one end user now has a Slack handle and an email address, which is
also the ordinary case an operator searches by.
M-I35 (removing the early return from `upsertByEmail`) survived because the
get-or-create has TWO independent defences and either one alone keeps the
ANSWER correct: the early return, and the unique-violation recovery around
the insert. That is a real property of the code and it is recorded rather
than papered over. The two halves were then separated so each is falsifiable
on its own -- M-I35 by a statement COUNT (a repeat login must cost ONE
statement, not a read, a refused insert and a second read) and M-I37 by
sixteen concurrent first logins for one address, which must produce one
account.
The first sweep of tranche 1 reported 22 kills that were ALL vacuous. This
sweep is the reason that cannot have happened again.
